rules.evidence_gate: Nothing is shown to the user as fact without verification.

questions.claim: duplicate / superseded files exist and can be quarantined
questions.verdict: Quarantined. 39 files moved to unnecessary/ incl. 0api.js, api.js.bak, zombie-gateway.js, old_local-llm-bridge.js, registry.db, registry.seed.json, 4 health-check jsons, 3 .bak files, legacy Test/ suite. Server healthy after move.
evidence: ps: only start.js + php-broker + 3 local MCP running

questions.claim: UDS is real and used headless (or nominal only)
questions.verdict: Inbound UDS is REAL and headless: api.js runs an MCP server on /tmp/zombiecoder/mcp.sock (net.createServer, mkdir dir, unlink stale socket, chmod 0660). Outbound UDS is supported (transport.js socketPath) but NOT configured: only custom providers can set it via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_N_SOCKET; BRIDGE_SOCKET in .env is commented out. Local Ollama speaks TCP 127.0.0.1:11434 (Ollama has no native UDS); local-llm-bridge.js can listen on UDS if BRIDGE_SOCKET is set.

questions.claim: external MCP boundary is deny-by-default and safe
questions.verdict: Safe TODAY by config: external mcp/servers.json holds only 3 loopback servers (ocr, screen-recorder, tts); EXTERNAL_MCP_URLS is unset; php-broker and appsp tool target 127.0.0.1. GAP: mcp-client.js accepts any http/https URL with no allowlist — the boundary is closed by config, not enforced by code. If remote MCP is ever enabled, add a deny-by-default allowlist first.
evidence: mcp-client.js:72 scheme check only, no host allowlist

questions.verdict: Correct and NOT blocking: atomic write via tmp+rename, 3-level backup rotation, pid-liveness lock + 30s staleness heuristic (stale lock self-heals), optional encryption, debounced flush. Lock owned by live PID 38645 at audit time. notes.json holds valid _meta (version 3.1.1, domain localhost).

questions.claim: tools resolve by path and new tools are registrable
questions.verdict: Yes. provider/tools.js is THE register (36 tools, DB capability gate, no hardcoded model names); external tools/servers.json is the descriptor table (file + actions + env) read by api.js; tool.js (UTCA) is a pure conversion library (765 lines, 8 dialects, selftest); a new tool = add a servers.json entry + module file under external tools/ — dispatcher untouched.
evidence: api.js:9766 tools from servers.json OR EXTERNAL_MCP_URLS
external tools/tool.js exports (converters only, no executor)

questions.claim: one authoritative persona source; others extra
questions.verdict: Runtime authority = SQLite agents table (admin CRUD persists there), seeded once from PERSONAS.md. agent/*.js are versioned code defaults (fallback when DB empty). PERSONAS.md is seed source + human doc. 3 representations of the same agents = real duplication. Recommended shape: one code source (agent/*.js as canonical seed) -> DB (runtime) -> PERSONAS.md generated for humans.

questions.claim: only transports actually spoken should be consolidated
questions.verdict: Transport consolidation ALREADY exists at provider/transport.js: https (HTTP/2 with HTTP/1.1 fallback), http (HTTP/1.1), UDS socketPath when configured. gRPC is spoken NOWHERE (zero references). Creating adapter/ with gRPC would be invention with no caller. Verdict: do NOT create adapter/; keep provider/transport.js as the single transport layer; add a gRPC adapter only when a real provider requires it.

questions.claim: editor clients can be served by thin adapters, core untouched
questions.verdict: The client layer ALREADY exists as config, not code: .missionbarisal/{mcp-config,vscode,jetbrains,editor-config}.json define endpoint/transport preferences (http :3000, uds /tmp/zombiecoder/mcp.sock, ws, stdio), and the server already exposes the OpenAI-compatible surface clients need: GET /v1/models, POST /v1/chat/completions, GET /api/v0/models, plus MCP. No new client/ code folder is justified; what is missing is per-editor DOCUMENTATION, not code.

questions.claim: configs load per run; port/env effects bounded
questions.verdict: Nothing boots with the OS: no .bashrc/.profile entries, no XDG autostart, no systemd unit, no crontab. Every run is manual `node start.js --start-all`. start.js CONFIG ALL writes ~/.zombiecoder/config.json (serverPort 3000, udsPath, workingDir). PORT from .env -> api.js PORT -> principled bindHost (loopback domain -> 127.0.0.1). Port change propagates to editor configs on next start.js run. We intentionally do not write .bashrc.

Tool COUNT is explicitly capped: MAX_TOOLS_LIMIT 25 (api.js:3639), local agents 5 / others 15 (api.js:14535+14550 slice), MAX_HISTORY 10, MAX_RECENT_CONTEXT 20, MAX_SAVED_CLIENTS 500. Stream bodies are accumulated UNBOUNDED (transport.js Buffer.concat / buf+=) and tool-call argument size is not capped — byte-level memory is bounded only by the process. Count-capped yes; byte-capped no (flag as risk, not a current bug).

Correct and zero-HTTP: cdp-pipe.js drives headless Chrome over --remote-debugging-pipe (fd 3 write / fd 4 read) with \0-framed CDP JSON both ways; no debug port/TCP/WS in the control channel. Used by api.js MCP tool browse_cdp. Passed the security verification suite.

questions.claim: personas map to real industry competencies
questions.verdict: Yes — personas carry concrete competencies + evidence-first decision rules: security-hero (OWASP, SQLi/XSS/CSRF, auth, data protection, CVE research before reporting), perf-wizard (profiling, caching, DB tuning, benchmark-gated recommendations), code-guru (architecture, module boundaries, design patterns, integration design). Note: agent/*.js display-name strings are Bengali by design (per PERSONAS.md constitution user-facing tone); identifiers/comments are English.

questions.claim: response logic enforceable at schema boundary
questions.verdict: provider/schema.json is NOT referenced by any runtime .js — shape validation lives in normalizer code. JSON Schema can enforce SHAPE (type/required/pattern/enum) at the adapter boundary (normalize-or-reject), but NOT logic (fallback hops, rate-limit cooldown, capability gates, provider priority) — that must stay imperative. Recommendation: keep logic in code; optionally wire schema.json as a reject-at-boundary validator per dialect.
evidence: grep schema.json: only docs/README/tests hits (docs/openai-schema.json is a different generated file)
normalizer/index.js does shape work in code

questions.claim: no watermark, no bias, no bypass, evidence-gated
questions.verdict: Clean. No watermark/bypass markers found; provider configs are symmetric (no per-provider consent; OpenCode headers live only in provider/opencode.js adapter); provider-level network-proxy code was removed in the prior session; capability lookup is DB-driven (no hardcoded model names — isLocalAgent uses config/local flag only). Evidence gate upheld: /health + E2E verify before/after quarantine.
